questions.q: How was David when he first came to himself on the ship?
choices: Tied to the mainmast while the sailors laughed at him
Lying on the deck in the sun with a cold wet cloth
Locked in the captain's cabin with a guard at the door
In darkness, in pain, and bound hand and foot
questions.evidence: I came to myself in darkness, in great pain, bound hand and foot

questions.q: Why was a gun fired as the brig passed Dysart?
choices: To signal the customs officers
The captain's mother lived there
The ship was in great danger
To warn other ships of the storm
questions.evidence: old Mrs. Hoseason, the captain's mother

questions.q: What does the gun fired for the captain's mother show about Hoseason, according to David?
choices: Even the worst man may have a kindlier side
He was afraid of being caught by the king's ships
He liked to frighten prisoners
He wanted the people of Dysart to see his wealth
questions.evidence: even the worst man may have his kindlier side

questions.q: Who was the small man with green eyes and fair hair who dressed David's wound?
choices: Captain Hoseason himself
Mr. Riach, the second officer
Mr. Shuan, the chief mate
Ransome, the cabin-boy
questions.evidence: I am no conjurer, Mr. Riach

questions.q: Mr. Riach calls David's wound "a sore dunt." Using the note in the text, what is a "dunt"?
choices: A rope burn on the wrists
A deep cut from a knife
A stroke or blow
A bad fever from the sea

questions.q: What frightened David while he lay in the dark hole of the ship?
choices: Rats scurrying, sometimes over his face
A strange voice singing from the darkness
Sailors coming down to beat him at night
Water slowly rising up around his feet
questions.evidence: the scurrying of the ship's rats, that sometimes pattered on my very face

questions.q: Where did Mr. Riach want David moved to?
choices: The round-house
The deck by the wheel
The captain's cabin
The forecastle
questions.evidence: I want that boy taken out of this hole and put in the forecastle

questions.q: What finally made the captain agree to move David?
choices: Riach said the lad would die if he stayed there
Riach offered to pay the captain with his own wages
The sailors threatened to stop work until he did
David promised to work hard as a ship's boy
questions.evidence: If ye say the lad will die

questions.q: When Mr. Riach says, "Admitting that you have been paid to do a murder," what is he hinting?
choices: That David's uncle had paid Riach to watch over him
That Mr. Shuan planned to murder the cabin-boy
That the captain had killed a sailor on a past voyage
That the captain was paid to get rid of David
questions.evidence: Admitting that you have been paid to do a murder

questions.q: Which sailor told David, "it was me that gave it ye," about the blow on his head?
choices: Mr. Riach as he dressed the wound
The man who brought him a healing drink
The captain on the night they sailed
Ransome when he came from the round-house
questions.evidence: it was me that gave it ye!

questions.q: How did David's opinion of the sailors change after living with them?
choices: He found that they were all honest men who had been kidnapped like him
He was ashamed of first thinking them wholly bad, since they had virtues
He decided they were cowards who were afraid of their cruel captain
He grew to hate them even more than on the day he first saw them at the pier
questions.evidence: I began to be ashamed of my first judgment

questions.q: Who would sit by David's berth for hours talking about his wife and child?
choices: The cook, once a soldier
A fisher who had lost his boat
A young sailor who had run from home
Mr. Riach, when he had been drinking
questions.evidence: He was a fisher that had lost his boat

questions.q: What good deed did the sailors do for David?
choices: They let him come up on deck every day to see the sea
They returned his money, though about a third was missing
They hid him from the captain whenever he came below
They taught him how to steer the ship through a storm
questions.evidence: they returned my money, which had been shared among them

questions.q: What did David's uncle mean to happen to him at the end of the voyage?
choices: To be handed over to soldiers as a rebel against the king
To be left on an island in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean
To be sold into slavery on the plantations in the Carolinas
To be trained as a sailor and work for Hoseason for life
questions.evidence: that was the destiny to which my wicked uncle had condemned me

questions.q: What was strange about the two mates, Mr. Riach and Mr. Shuan?
choices: Both had once been pirates and had sailed under the black flag
Riach was harsh when sober; Shuan was gentle unless drinking
Both were kind when sober and cruel whenever they drank
Riach could not sail; Shuan could not read or write
questions.evidence: Mr. Riach was sullen, unkind, and harsh when he was sober

questions.q: What could Ransome remember of his life before he went to sea?
choices: He had lived on a farm and looked after the sheep
His father made clocks and had a whistling starling
He had gone to school and learned to read and write
His mother sang to him in a little house by a river
questions.evidence: only that his father had made clocks

choices: Mr. Shuan
The captain
The sailors
Mr. Riach
questions.evidence: It was Mr. Riach (Heaven forgive him!) who gave the boy drink

questions.q: What did Mr. Riach promise after David told him his whole story?
choices: To ask the captain to turn the ship around and take him home at once
To help him jump overboard and swim to the nearest shore at night
To get him pen and paper to write to Mr. Campbell and Mr. Rankeillor
To hide him in the round-house until they reached the Carolinas
questions.evidence: I should have paper, pen, and ink, and write one line to Mr. Campbell

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David's daring escape from the Covenant during a great storm at sea
David's quarrel with the captain over the money his uncle paid
David's first days as a prisoner on the Covenant and the people he meets there
David's arrival in the Carolinas and his sale to a planter
questions.evidence: Here I lay for the space of many days a close prisoner
